title: Possessor forms with singular owners
summary: One owner uses a learned possessor form: minulla, sinulla, and hänellä.
objectives: One owner uses a learned possessor form: minulla, sinulla, and hänellä.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: One owner uses a learned possessor form: minulla, sinulla, and hänellä.
Minä → minulla, sinä → sinulla, hän → hänellä. Learn these forms as whole pronoun forms, rather than attaching an ending directly to the subject pronoun.
Hänellä can refer to a man or a woman. Sinulla addresses one informal listener.
keyPoints: One owner uses a learned possessor form: minulla, sinulla, and hänellä.

steps: Start from minä (“I”) and learn its owner form minulla. Do not attach -lla directly to minä.
The shown on supplies “have” in this possession pattern.
pallo names one ball; put it after on.
The shown on supplies “have” in this possession pattern.
kirja names one book; put it after on.
Hän (“he” or “she”) has the owner form hänellä. Gender does not change that Finnish form.
The shown on supplies “has” in this possession pattern.
koira names one dog; put it after on.
Reuse minulla for the same owner with a different thing; the noun does not change the owner form.
The shown on supplies “have” in this possession pattern.
kissa names one cat; put it after on.

commonMistakes: Use minulla for “I have”, rather than the subject pronoun minä. Learn the pronoun forms as a table; minä + -lla does not give minulla.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Choose the possessor form for “I have a pen.” Frame: “___ on kynä.” Use kynä (“a pen”) and on (“have/has”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Use minulla, the possession form of minä. The owner comes before fixed on.

optionFeedback.minulla: Use minulla, the possession form of minä. The owner comes before fixed on.
optionFeedback.sinulla: sinulla identifies you as the owner; the requested owner is I.
optionFeedback.hänellä: hänellä identifies he as the owner; the requested owner is I.
optionFeedback.meillä: meillä identifies we as the owner; the requested owner is I.
optionFeedback.teillä: teillä identifies you as the owner; the requested owner is I.
optionFeedback.heillä: heillä identifies they as the owner; the requested owner is I.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: possessor + fixed on + one thing in its basic singular form

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: minä has the learned possession form minulla; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Olla means “to be”; possession uses fixed on with minulla, sinulla and hänellä.
kynä stays in its basic singular form: one pen.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: The basic personal pronoun identifies a subject. Possession needs the learned -lla/-llä owner form shown by the lesson.
